content.text:
This version leaves the "Run code tasks in a container" option as it is, since you didn't say to drop it. The code lane gets a sessions folder only for the case where that option is on.

---

> Keep each project's containerized harness sessions in the project itself, so a conversation carries on across runs, restarts, and moves of the project.
>
> **ContainerEnvironmentScope, Volumes:** the harness's sessions for each conversation are no longer kept in Podman volumes. They are kept in the project, in `.suspense/sessions/`, one folder per conversation: `spec` for the spec lane, `questions` for the Ask tab's questions, and `code` for the code lane while the project's "Run code tasks in a container" option is on. Each run mounts only its own conversation's folder, read and write, where the harness keeps its sessions under its home, never `.suspense/sessions/` as a whole, so no run sees another conversation's sessions. The application creates the folder before the run if it isn't there. The harness's login and settings stay in one volume per harness, shared by every project, and the project's caches stay in their volume, as now. Losing the project's sessions folder costs only the conversations' context: the next run starts a new conversation, as when a session can't be resumed. Sessions kept in volumes before this aren't carried over; each conversation starts fresh.
>
> **Volume names:** the project's cache volume is named after an ID the project keeps, not after its path. The ID is generated once, the first time the project needs one, and kept in `.suspense/project-id`, so renaming or moving the project keeps its volume. A name never depends on a hash whose algorithm may change between versions of the application.
>
> **ContainerEnvironmentScope, Mounts and Paths:** the project is mounted at the same fixed path in the container, `/workspace`, on every platform, and the run works there, so a harness that keys its sessions on its working directory, as Claude Code does, finds them again after the project moves. Change Mounts so it no longer says each location is mounted at its host path where the platform allows. Paths now applies on every platform: every path a run reports is mapped back to its host path before it is shown or opened. Only a path that is `/workspace` or begins with `/workspace/` is mapped, never text that merely contains it, as `/workspace-old`. A path that maps to nothing on the host is shown as the run gave it, and opens nothing, as now.
>
> **ProjectDataScope:** add `.suspense/sessions/` and `.suspense/project-id` to the project data. Both belong to this machine: git ignores them and they are never committed, since the sessions hold the harness's transcripts. Change the paragraph that says the harnesses' sessions aren't in `.suspense`: the images, logins, and caches still aren't, but the sessions now are.
>
> **HarnessIntegrationScope:** a conversation is only carried on where it began, in a container or on the host. Which of the two it began in is kept beside it in `.suspense/conversations.json`, so a project reopened after a restart never tries to resume a conversation in the other place. A conversation whose place isn't known, as one from older history, is tried, and if the harness has no such session, it is sent again at once as a new conversation, as now.

---

If you'd rather drop code containerization altogether, remove the `code` folder clause and the "Volume names" section. Without Code runs in containers there's no cache volume, so no project volume is left to name.
